chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Amr ibn Shimir, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I lick my fingers from the sauce until I fear that my servant will see me, and he will think that this is from greed, and that is not so.'

Indeed, a people upon whom blessings were poured, and they are the people of Tharthar, so they took the core of the wheat and made it bread for firewood, and they used it to clean their children with, until a great mountain gathered from that.

He said: So a righteous man passed by them, and there was a woman, and she was doing that with a child of hers. So he said to them, 'Woe to you! Fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and do not change what is with you from the blessings.' So she said to him, 'It is as if you are frightening us with hunger. But as long as our Tharthar is flowing, we do not fear hunger.'

He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made them regret, and He weakened the Tharthar for them, and withheld from them the drops of the sky and the vegetation of the earth. He said: So they became in need of that mountain, and it was distributed among them by the scale.

key_terms.التَّجَشُّع: Greed or gluttony (literally belching, used here metaphorically for excessive consumption/waste)
key_terms.الثَّرْثَار: Tharthar (a river or water source, specifically referring to the Tigris or a local river known for abundance)
key_terms.الْجَبَل: Mountain (referring to a large accumulated pile)
key_terms.مُخِّ الْحِنْطَة: The core/center of the wheat (referring to the best part)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the people of Tharthar and how does it illustrate gratitude and waste?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the virtue of frugality by contrasting the Prophet’s modest habit of licking his fingers to avoid wasting even a grain of bread with the extravagance of the 'people of Tharthar.' It serves as a practical lesson on avoiding *israf* (waste) and *ungratefulness*, illustrating how divine blessings can be withdrawn when their purpose is misused, leading to scarcity despite initial abundance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Amro Bin Shimr who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> lick my<sup>asws</sup> fingers from the sauce until I<sup>asws</sup> fear that my<sup>asws</sup> servant would see me, so he would view that as being from the greed, and that is not like that.

A people had the Bounties offloaded upon them, and they are the (people of) Sarsaar. So they took the wheat and made it as bread (to be used) for firewood, and made it to be utilised for cleaning their children with it, to the extent that a big hill gathered from that (soiled bread)’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So a righteous man passed by them and there was a woman, and she was doing that with a child of hers (cleaning him with the bread). So he said to them, ‘Woe be unto you all! Fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Might and Majestic, and do not change what is with you from the Bounties’. So she said to him, ‘It is as if you are scaring us with the hunger. But, for as long as our Sarsaar (river) is flowing, so we do not fear the hunger’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Made them regret and weakened the Sarsaar (river) to them, and Withheld the drops of the sky (rain) from them, and the vegetation of the earth. So they became needy to that hill (of soiled bread) and they would then distribute it between them with the scale’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘ Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah ‘Amr ibn Shamir who has said the following:
“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I lick food from my fingers but I fear my servants’ seeing me and their thinking that I am greedy. That is not true.
A people upon whom bounties were poured owned a very large canal. They bleached the wheat for bread for food and used it to wipe their children with it until the dumpsite became like a huge mountain.

A virtuous man passed by and saw a woman wipe her child with it. He said to them, ‘Fie upon you, have fear of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, and do not change the bounty you enjoy.’ She said, ‘Are you frightening us of hunger? As long as we have our great canal flowing we will not be afraid of hunger.’

It angered Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, and He made their canal to weaken, stopped the sky to rain on them and the earth to grow (anything ). He (the Imam) said, ‘They became needy of that dumpsite and divided it among them by means of balance.’”
